questionText:
Read the following passage carefully and answer the question that follows:

"On 12 June 1975, Justice Jagmohan Lal Sinha of the Allahabad High Court delivered a sensational verdict unseating Prime Minister Indira Gandhi, finding her guilty of electoral malpractices in Rae Bareli. On 24 June, Supreme Court vacation judge Justice V.R. Krishna Iyer granted only a conditional stay. Faced with calls for her resignation, on the night of 25 June 1975, Indira Gandhi advised President Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed to proclaim a National Emergency under Article 352 on the subjective grounds of 'internal disturbance'. Before the Union Cabinet was even informed, electricity to major newspaper printing presses in Delhi was severed, and top opposition leaders—including JP, Morarji Desai, and Atal Bihari Vajpayee—were arrested under MISA. Fundamental rights were suspended, strict press censorship was imposed, and extra-constitutional power was wielded by Sanjay Gandhi, who enforced ruthless slum demolitions at Turkman Gate and coercive sterilization quotas. In April 1976, in the infamous ADM Jabalpur v. Shivkant Shukla (Habeas Corpus) case, the Supreme Court four-judge majority disgracefully ruled that citizens could not approach courts for protection of life or liberty during Emergency. Only Justice H.R. Khanna courageously dissented, defending inviolable human liberty."

questionText:
Which among the following statements are correct about the economic
consequences of globalisation?

options.text:
The economic flows among different nations of the world are
involuntary and are all forced by international organizations.

options.text:
Globalisation has led to greater interdependence and integration
between governments, businesses and ordinary people in different parts of
the world. 
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
 
1. (A) and (B) only
2. (C) and (D) only
3. (B) and (D) only
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

options.text:
Globalization has led to the adoption of similar economic policies by
governments in different parts of the world and generated the same

options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately identifies the chronological/logical progression.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
Evaluation of economic globalization statements:
- (A) Incorrect: Economic flows are not all involuntary or forced by international organizations; many sovereign states voluntarily deregulate to attract foreign capital and technology.
- (B) Correct: Globalization has dramatically dismantled barriers and tariffs on cross-border capital mobility and foreign direct investment.
- (C) Incorrect: While similar market deregulation was adopted, it produced vastly UNEQUAL and divergent outcomes, creating winners and losers rather than 'the same outcomes in all countries'.
- (D) Correct: Globalization has woven intricate webs of mutual interdependence and economic integration across governments, corporations, and citizens.
Hence, statements (B) and (D) only are correct.
Hence, option (D) is correct.

questionText:
Arrange the events related to the founding of the United Nations (UN) in chronological order.

(A) India joined the UN
(B) Tehran Conference Declaration of the Three Powers (US, Britain and Soviet Union)
(C) Signing of the Atlantic Charter by the US President Franklin D. Roosevelt and British PM Winston S. Churchill
(D) The UN was founded

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.
Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.
Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.
Correct answer. Accurately identifies the chronological/logical progression.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
NCERT Class 12 Contemporary World Politics (Chapter 6: International Organisations, 'Declaration and Evolution of the UN' timeline, p. 83): (C) Signing of the Atlantic Charter by FDR and Churchill took place in August 1941. (B) Declaration of the Three Powers at the Tehran Conference occurred in December 1943. (D) The United Nations was officially founded on 24 October 1945 when the Charter was ratified. (A) India joined the UN as an original founding member on 30 October 1945. Chronological sequence: (C) [1941] -> (B) [1943] -> (D) [24 Oct 1945] -> (A) [30 Oct 1945].
Hence, option (D) is correct.
